incident-bot: URGENT: latency spike detected for model-serving-prod [p95/p99 SLO breach]
Maya: I'm on it. seeing alerts too. p95 2.3s, p99 5.8s, streaming stalls ~12% last 5m :grimacing:
Liam: linking dashboards -> https://internal.redwood/dashboards/serving/kv-cache-pressure
Sanjay: hitting it now, looks like KV cache eviction rate jumped ~50->820/s around 14:03 UTC
Maya: can someone check prefill hit ratio? I suspect prefill vs decode imbalance
Tasha: prefill hit rate dropped from 92% -> 46% at the spike, decode time p99 hopped from 120ms -> 1.9s
Natalie: I'm seeing fragmentation warnings in allocator logs, glibc malloc failed compaction hints
Maya: copying logs:
```
[14:03:12] kv_cache: eviction: key=slot_0x7f4ff type=prefill size=128k
[14:03:12] allocator: frag_ratio=0.72, free_pages=120MB
[14:03:13] decode: stall=1.1s req_id=abc123 stream_id=stream-789
```
Liam: +1 on fragmentation. Looks like prefill processes are holding many small allocations causing heap fragmentation; eviction thrashing
Maya: customer impact? CS-bot, any affected customers reported?
CS-bot: Notified customers: acct-5688 (high qps), acct-2102 (streaming), acct-7701 (background). CS assigned to notify major customers, initial ETA T+30m
Sanjay: quick mitigation proposals:
- reduce prefill concurrency from 6 -> 2 on the hot pool
- temporarily increase eviction threshold to prefer LRU over sampling
- scale dedicated pool gp1-hot +1 instance
Maya: fine with that. Liam, can you push the prefill concurrency change to prod via runtime flag?
Liam: pushing now via config manager
```
PATCH /runtime/config/model-serving
{ "prefill_concurrency": 2 }
```
ops-bot: Deploy triggered by Liam at 14:08 UTC (deploy-id: dpl-3341)
Tasha: scaling hot pool now (requested +1 GPU), expected to be ready in ~3m
Maya: also enabling temporary route fallback for streaming routes to model-small-v2 for requests > 2s
Liam: fallback rule applied: if backend latency >1500ms route -> model-small-v2
Sanjay: after changes: eviction/sec dropped to ~120, prefill hit rate climbed to 78%, p95 down to 320ms, p99 720ms
Maya: streaming stalls reduced to ~2.5% in the last 3m :thumbsup:
Natalie: added a monitoring alert to detect frag_ratio > 0.6 and eviction/sec > 200
Maya: Postmortem action items:
- (#1) investigate allocator fragmentation root cause (memory allocator, prefill buffer sizes)
- (#2) add proactive compaction or jemalloc for prefill processes
- (#3) tune eviction policy to be more conservative under bursty workloads
- (#4) run chaos test for prefill vs decode imbalance
- (#5) customer comms draft (CS)
Liam: handing off to next on-call @Sanjay for the rest of the cleanup and postmortem
Sanjay: taking handoff. will keep monitoring for 2 hours and then transition to eng-sre ticketing
Maya: leaving notes in incident ticket: https://internal.redwood/incidents/2323456789-kv-evict-frag
ops-bot: Incident status -> mitigated, impact reduced. Open action items: 5
Natalie: assigning owners: allocator research (Natalie), eviction tuning (Maya), chaos test (Liam), CS comms (Natalie)
Maya: thanks all. if anything regress ping me @Maya. closing slack thread once postmortem PR is opened :eyes:
CS-bot: Customers notified (initial): acct-5688 (high qps) updated at 14:20 UTC
Sanjay: last check: p95 280ms, p99 640ms, streaming stalls 1.8% over 15m window
Maya: Marking as resolved on slack - followups in incident ticket. Great job team :partyparrot:
